SUMMARY AND BACKGROUND 
The City of Berkeley has faced a persistent General Fund structural deficit for many years. 
The upcoming FY 2027–FY 2028 Biennial Budget continues this trend but with a critical shift. 
Rather than relying on one-time fixes, the proposed Budget Balancing Plan recommends 
long‑term, structural adjustments to restore fiscal stability1. 
The City’s financial outlook reflects the following: 
 Ongoing structural General Fund deficit

L18: The Campus is an interim housing site from Insight Housing (formerly Berkley Food & Housing Project) and the City of Berkeley. The Campus is located in the former Super 8 Motel on Berkeley’s University Avenue, and is part of the City’s plan to provide stable housing and case management services to people experiencing homelessness, particularly those who have been living in encampments.
L19: The site offers 23 private rooms, each with a bathroom, television, microwave, and mini-fridge, and a variety of other services including security, twice weekly housekeeping, and three meals per day. To support their comfort and independence, residents are allowed to bring their pets and have the freedom to come and go without a curfew.
L20: Residents of the campus are able to stay as long as necessary to find permanent housing, and are guided and supported by case workers with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. The Campus’ annual cost of $2.54 million will be supplemented by Berekely’s Measure P in 2026 through June 30, 2027.
